## Natural history notes

A small tumbling flower beetle characterized by its wedge-shaped body, dark coloration, pale or blister-like spots, and pointed abdomen that gives many mordellid beetles a hunched, tumbling appearance. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, parks, roadsides, and other open or semi-open habitats with flowering plants and nearby dead wood or plant stems. Adults visit flowers for pollen or nectar and may tumble or spring away when disturbed, while the larvae develop in dead wood, stems, or decaying plant material, helping recycle plant tissue and contributing to the broader insect food web.
